title: до того как, после того как, о том что…

blocks.text: Every Russian preposition demands a noun in a special case. But sometimes a preposition refers not to a single noun, but to a clause, thus forming a complex sentence: a) *Мы успели приехать домой до начала грозы.* (simple sentence) b) *Мы успели приехать домой до того, как гроза началась.* (complex sentence)
When a preposition refers to a whole clause, a complex conjunction is used consisting of: 1) the preposition, 2) the pronoun "то" in the case required by the preposition, 3) a linking word.

Examples: *Они ушли из дома до того, как в него попала бомба. Я расскажу вам о том, что было на собрании.* Complex conjunctions have to be used when the preposition refers to a clause. However it is preferable to avoid them if the meaning of the clause can be clearly expressed by a simple preposition and a noun: *Мы все поедем в Европу после окончания школы.*
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 92.

The exercises are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. The word in brackets is the dictionary form of the missing word.
